title: GCN Builds and Reviews a Bamboo Bike
body_html:
The Global Cycling Network — one of the largest cycling channels in the world — came to Bamboo Bicycle Club to build a bamboo frame from scratch and put it to the test.

Their presenters worked through the whole process: selecting the bamboo, setting up the jig, and turning a bundle of canes into a complete, rideable frame. The finished gravel build was set up for 650B × 47mm tyres and taken out across mixed terrain to see how it holds up against the claims people make about bamboo as a frame material.

The takeaway was the one our builders have known for over a decade: a well-built bamboo frame is a genuinely capable bike, with its own ride character — not a novelty.

Bamboo's appeal here comes down to comfort. As road.cc put it in their December 2020 build feature, bamboo offers "excellent vibration dampening effects" alongside good stress resistance and durability — which is exactly why it suits gravel, where the surface is unpredictable and comfort over distance matters.

This is the same coverage as our main write-up. For the full build-and-review, see
GCN Build and Review a Bamboo Gravel Bike.
